ultra-rapid metabolizer.recommendation: SLCO1B1 is a transporter gene — no ultra-rapid phenotype defined. Recommend SLCO1B1 genotyping if not already performed. If SLCO1B1 normal function, prescribe desired starting dose per disease-specific guidelines.

normal metabolizer.recommendation: Prescribe desired starting dose and adjust doses based on disease-specific guidelines.

intermediate metabolizer.recommendation: Increased simvastatin acid exposure as compared to normal function; increased risk of myopathy. Prescribe an alternative statin depending on desired potency. If simvastatin warranted, limit dose to <20 mg/day.

poor metabolizer.recommendation: Highly increased simvastatin acid exposure; highly increased myopathy risk. Prescribe an alternative statin depending on desired potency.

ultra-rapid metabolizer.recommendation: SLCO1B1 is a transporter gene — no ultra-rapid phenotype defined. Recommend SLCO1B1 genotyping if not already performed. If SLCO1B1 normal function, prescribe desired starting dose per disease-specific guidelines.

normal metabolizer.recommendation: Prescribe desired starting dose and adjust doses based on disease-specific guidelines.

intermediate metabolizer.recommendation: Increased atorvastatin exposure as compared to normal function which may translate to increased myopathy risk. Prescribe ≤40 mg as a starting dose. Prescriber should be aware of possible increased risk for myopathy especially for 40 mg dose. If >40 mg needed, consider combination therapy.

poor metabolizer.recommendation: Increased atorvastatin exposure as compared to normal and decreased function which may translate to increased myopathy risk. Prescribe ≤20 mg as a starting dose. If >20 mg needed, consider rosuvastatin or combination therapy.

ultra-rapid metabolizer.recommendation: SLCO1B1 is a transporter gene — no ultra-rapid phenotype defined. Recommend SLCO1B1 and ABCG2 genotyping if not already performed. If SLCO1B1 normal function and ABCG2 normal function, prescribe desired starting dose per disease-specific guidelines.

normal metabolizer.recommendation: Prescribe desired starting dose and adjust doses based on disease-specific and specific population guidelines.

intermediate metabolizer.recommendation: Increased rosuvastatin exposure as compared to normal function. Prescribe desired starting dose. Prescriber should be aware of possible increased risk for myopathy especially for doses >20 mg. If ABCG2 decreased function also present, consider moderate recommendation.
intermediate metabolizer.source: CPIC (Strong for SLCO1B1 alone; Moderate for ABCG2)

poor metabolizer.recommendation: Increased rosuvastatin exposure as compared to normal function. Prescribe ≤20 mg as a starting dose. If dose >20 mg needed for desired efficacy, consider combination therapy. If combined with ABCG2 poor function, starting dose ≤10 mg.
poor metabolizer.source: CPIC (Moderate for SLCO1B1; Optional for ABCG2)

ultra-rapid metabolizer.recommendation: SLCO1B1 is a transporter gene — no ultra-rapid phenotype defined. Recommend SLCO1B1 and CYP2C9 genotyping if not already performed. If SLCO1B1 normal function and CYP2C9 normal metabolizer, prescribe desired starting dose per disease-specific guidelines.

normal metabolizer.recommendation: Prescribe desired starting dose and adjust doses based on disease-specific guidelines.

intermediate metabolizer.recommendation: Increased fluvastatin exposure as compared to normal metabolizer which may translate to increased myopathy risk. Prescribe ≤40 mg per day as a starting dose. If dose >40 mg needed, consider alternative statin or combination therapy. If combined with SLCO1B1 decreased/poor function, highest risk.

poor metabolizer.recommendation: Increased fluvastatin exposure as compared to normal and intermediate metabolizer which may translate to increased myopathy risk. Prescribe ≤20 mg per day as a starting dose. If dose >20 mg needed, consider alternative statin or combination therapy. If combined with SLCO1B1 decreased/poor function, use alternative agent.
